args.title: Fix weekly rollup schedule to honour non-hour time zone offsets
args.body:
File: src/notifications/rollup.ts

startRollupSchedule only ticks at the top of each UTC hour (every HOUR_MS, aligned to Date.now() % HOUR_MS). For time zones whose UTC offset isn't a whole number of hours (Asia/Kolkata +5:30, America/St_Johns -3:30, Asia/Kathmandu +5:45), none of those ticks land on local :00, so isRollupDue's hour check is first satisfied 15-45 minutes late, which is exactly the 08:30/08:45 delivery reported.

Change the schedule to tick at a finer granularity (every 15 minutes, since IANA offsets are always multiples of 15 minutes) and tighten isRollupDue (or add a minute check) so each user is still only sent one rollup per week despite the more frequent ticks.

file: src/notifications/rollup.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The rollup scheduler ticks only at the top of each UTC hour (startRollupSchedule's setInterval(HOUR_MS, ...)). For time zones whose offset from UTC isn't a whole number of hours — Asia/Kolkata (+5:30), America/St_Johns (-3:30), Asia/Kathmandu (+5:45) — none of those hourly ticks land exactly on local :00, so isRollupDue's local-hour check first comes true 15-45 minutes into the hour, which matches the 08:30/08:30/08:45 deliveries reported. London and Chicago, both whole-hour offsets, are unaffected. The fix is to tick more often (every 15 minutes covers all real IANA offsets) and make sure each user still only gets one send per week.
